Question kind: control_flow_prediction

Question:
Use `tests/qa/testcase.py`, class `TestLanguageExtensionsFindInMapDefaultInitReachabilityQA`, method `test_language_extensions_findinmap_default_init_reachability_case`. The test instantiates `cfnlint.template.transforms._language_extensions._Transform` and runs `transform(cfn)` over `_TEMPLATE`. Question: during this test execution, is `cfnlint.template.transforms._language_extensions._FnFindInMapDefaultValue.__init__` EVER called (one or more times)? Return the answer under the field `is_reached` as a boolean. Reasoning rules to simulate: (1) `_FnFindInMapDefaultValue.__init__` is invoked at line 312 of `_language_extensions.py`, INSIDE `_ForEachValueFnFindInMap.__init__`, ONLY when the Fn::FindInMap argument list has length 4 (the optional DefaultValue object). (2) `_ForEachValueFnFindInMap.__init__` itself is invoked either directly by `_walk` (its `Fn::FindInMap` dispatch arm at line 161-174) or transitively when `_ForEachValue.create({"Fn::FindInMap": [...]})` is called (e.g. for a nested FindInMap). Either way, the FindInMap dict must be REACHED by `_walk`. (3) `_walk`'s `Fn::ToJsonString` dispatch arm at line 141-143 short-circuits: it returns the deepcopied dict WITHOUT recursing into the value. So any FindInMap buried inside an `Fn::ToJsonString` value is never walked, never constructed, and DefaultValue.__init__ is never reached from there. (4) A 3-element FindInMap (no DefaultValue) does NOT trigger DefaultValue.__init__, regardless of how many times the FindInMap itself is constructed -- the `if len(obj) == 4:` guard at line 311 prevents it. (5) The Fn::ForEach iteration walks the body once per collection element.

Template answer (must match exactly):
{"is_reached":"bool"}

- files/tests/qa/testcase.py

I have the key `_walk` logic:

- `transform()` returns `self._walk(cfn.template, {}, cfn)`.
- In `_walk`, when iterating a dict:
  - `Fn::ForEach` expands by iterating `foreach.items(...)` and recursively walking the body `v[2]` once per collection value.
  - `Fn::ToJsonString` immediately returns the object unchanged, with no recursion into its value.
  - `Fn::FindInMap` constructs `_ForEachValueFnFindInMap(get_hash(v), v)`, then tries to resolve it; if unresolved it recursively walks each element of the list.
So the question reduces to whether any walked `Fn::FindInMap` has a 4-element list. I still need the constructor code for `_ForEachValueFnFindInMap` and `_FnFindInMapDefaultValue`, plus `_ForEach.items` to confirm the body is walked twice for `["X", "Y"]`.
